title: Butler Tract Building OK'd with Utility Rules
summary:
*   City leaders debated the ideal location for a new Chamber of Commerce building on the Butler Tract.
*   City staff suggested moving the building for easier and cheaper utility access, but Chamber representatives argued against it due to the existing design tailored for the specific site, secured financing, and already-taken construction bids.
*   The council informally approved the Chamber of Commerce's preferred building location and submitted plans.
*   This approval came with conditions: water for air conditioning would come from a well, telephone and electric lines would be buried underground, and the Chambers of Commerce would pay for their own water and sewer line extensions.

September 2, 1958
3:00 Ρ.Μ.
Council Chamber, City Hall
The meeting was called to order with Mayor Miller presiding. Roll call: Present:
Councilmen Palmer, White, Mayor Miller
Absent: Councilmen Long, Pearson
Present also: W. T. Williams, Jr., City Manager; Doren R. Eskew, City Attorney Present
from the Chambers of Commerce were MR. REX SHIELDS, MR. KENT RIDER, MR. LOUIS GOLDBERG,
MR. VIC MATHIAS, and MR. MOTON CROCKETT, JR., and other members, and the Architect.
The Mayor announced that this was a Special Meeting called for the purpose of discussing
with the representatives of the Chamber of Commerce and of the Junior Chamber of Commerce
the location of the building on the Butler Tract.
The City Manager displayed maps showing proposed development of the tract of the
Auditorium, and suggested that the Chambers of Commerce might want to relocate the
building where it would have access to Barton Springs Road, and where the utility
extensions would not be so expensive.
Members from the Chambers of Commerce stated the building had been designed for this
particular, oddly shaped piece of ground; that the airconditioning had been planned for
this location, and the building had been designed so that there would be a view of the
City and of the Auditorium from both the Junior Chamber of Commerce quarters, and the
Chamber of Commerce quarters. It was the request of the group that no delay be made in the
construction, as bids had already been taken, and the financing had been arranged. If the
building had to be redesigned, the bids might not be the same. It was stated that the
delay in redesigning the building and taking new bids would be more costly than running
the utility lines.
The Council went over the plans for the building with the Architect.
The Mayor suggested that Mr. Sutherland work with Mr. Jessen on the landscaping of the
area. The Council informally approved the plans as submitted, and stated
